concepts.label: Built-in Administrator account
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - this page states there is exactly ONE built-in Administrator account, 'managed separately from the internal and external Administrator users' (i.e. separately from ordinary server:user records in auth-domain:local or auth-domain:external). relations.subject: server:built-in-administrator-account
relations.evidence: There is only one built-in Administrator account, which is managed separately from the internal and external Administrator users. External and internal Administrator accounts can be managed using the [user-manage](couchbase-cli-user-manage.md) command.

relations.subject: tool:couchbase-cli-reset-admin-password
relations.reused_or_minted_predicate: reused - closest existing predicate for the stated local-token authorization fact; see notable_absence
relations.evidence: The `reset-admin-password` command must be run locally on a node that is part of the cluster (i.e. must connect to the host the command is run on). This is required, as `reset-admin-password` relies on a local authentication token, which is used to authenticate with the server and change the password. As a result, the command does not require credentials to be passed.

notable_absence.finding: Like master-password, this command's authorization model is explicitly non-RBAC ('the command does not require credentials to be passed', relying instead on 'a local authentication token'). No role:/privilege: concept is invoked anywhere on the page - unusual in a batch this RBAC-dense: resetting the single most powerful account in the cluster is gated purely by local filesystem/node access, not by any Server RBAC role.

cross_component_finding: This page and admin-manage.md (also in this batch) share a near-verbatim paragraph almost word for word: 'There is only one built-in Administrator account, which is managed separately from the internal and external Administrator users. External and internal Administrator accounts can be managed using the [user-manage] command' appears on both pages, as does the 'must be run locally on a node that is part of the cluster ... relies on a local authentication token ... does not require credentials to be passed' paragraph (with only the specific verb changed - 'change the password' here vs 'perform actions such as locking the user' on admin-manage.md). This is exactly the flag-descriptions-copy-pasted-across-near-identical-siblings pattern this round's framing predicted for lightly-reviewed, engineer-authored CLI reference pages.
cross_product_finding: n/a - no Capella/Mobile/SDK content on this page; the built-in Administrator account and its local-token reset mechanism are Server-only concepts with no stated Capella management-plane equivalent.
